a13.source: CENTS Lab Market, screenshot supplied by the user 2026-10-06
a13.subject: Screenshot of the CENTS Lab Market: a filter panel over a grid of individually photographed Lincoln cents, each labelled with its CENT number (#8969, #8972, #8541 ...) and a price in bitcoin (0.00366 B, 0.00367 B ...). 'Hits: 198' and 'On Sale' are set, so what is shown is the set's members currently listed for sale.
a13.rights: screenshot of the CENTS Lab Market interface, supplied by the essay's author; depicts Rutherford Chang's CENTS being offered for sale
a13.crop_restrictions: Screenshot of a real interface. The row of coins WITH their numbers and prices is the content - a crop that keeps the coins but loses the prices turns a market into a contact sheet. Crop declared below keeps coin, id and price, and excludes the 'Open CENTS Bot' overlay at lower right, which is chat furniture and not the work.

a14.source: Rutherford Chang's workspace and the casting of the CENTS Block; supplied by the essay's author 2026-10-07
a14.subject: Footage of the CENTS Block being cast outdoors: a crucible of molten copper is tilted on a pivoting arm and poured in a bright orange stream into a square mould built of white refractory brick, smoke rising as it fills. Two figures in heat suits and face shields work the crucible. 8s excerpt from a 110s clip, starting at 76.0s, which is where the tilt and the pour are.
a14.rights: photographs and footage of Rutherford Chang's studio process, supplied by the essay's author for use in films about CENTS
a14.crop_restrictions: Vertical 480x848 and that is its real resolution, not a thumbnail. Do not display wider than ~560px: at full canvas width it is a 2.25x upscale and goes to mush. Never crop to the stream alone - the mould is what the copper is becoming, and losing it turns a casting into a fire.
a14.identified_by: claude, by viewing sampled frames across the source clip
